mission_08: Advanced quantum data encoding strategies go beyond simple angle encoding to create richer quantum representations. Basis encoding maps integers to computational basis states (sparse but exact). Dense angle encoding packs two features per qubit using RY and RZ rotations (efficient use of qubits). Tree tensor encoding creates hierarchical entanglement patterns through a tree-structured CNOT network (captures multi-scale correlations). Hamiltonian encoding simulates time evolution under a data-dependent Hamiltonian H = sum(x_i * Z_i) + sum(x_i * x_j * Z_i * Z_j), creating the most expressive encoding by leveraging both single-body and two-body interactions. In this mission, you implement all four encoding strategies, compute their properties (nonzero amplitudes, Shannon entropy), and compare their expressivity for the same input data.
